0be308cb-4508-4daf-98ef-9fc53ced79b8.quote: Defensible keep, with one conditional swap. If Greystone's or Kira's healing is what keeps fights alive, Tainted Rounds in Demolisher's slot puts 45% healing reduction on every basic attack and adds damage as the target's health drops; it gives up some physical power and Demolisher's armor ignore. Against a lobby with no armor buyers and a heavy-healing jungler, that trade leans toward Tainted Rounds the next time the enemy looks like this.

Keep Tainted Scepter whenever the enemy jungler or carry heals heavily, as Greystone and Kira did here. If a future enemy instead locks down our carry with stuns and roots, Enra's Blessing in Prophecy's slot shields immobilized allies nearby; it trades Phase's own on-hit damage and attack speed for protection she cannot otherwise provide. Nothing in this match proves that swap was needed.

0be308cb-4508-4daf-98ef-9fc53ced79b8.quote: Krix grows maximum health with level. Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after eight seconds without hero damage, and Cannibalism adds permanent health on takedowns, a lane-sustain setup. Offlane Steel players more often pair Voracity with Cannibalism. Festering Wounds would make Steel's stuns and knockups cut enemy healing by 45%, giving up Regenerative Tissue's recovery between trades for anti-heal on Greystone and Scarlett.

Fire Blossom burns nearby enemies with damage that ramps the longer it sticks, and Tainted Guard puts 45% healing reduction and a bleed on anyone who basic attacks Steel. Against Scarlett's omnivamp and Greystone's healing, Tainted Guard has a clear trigger. Both items stack bonus armor, though, and Infernum turns bonus armor into extra ignite damage. Flux Matrix, the missing core piece, adds magical armor and makes nearby enemies take more magic damage.
